_readme: THE SERVED-CHANNEL REGISTER — [pipeline R-5] company/pipeline/09-release-engineering.md
The complete set of channels this factory can release to: what artifact each one accepts, what
signing identity it needs, which lane produces it, which toolchain floor gates it, and — the field
everything else hangs off — whether it is SERVED today.
WHY IT EXISTS. Nine acceptance criteria across stages 9 and 10 quantify over 'the served set', and
until this file landed that set did not exist. An undefined right-hand side cannot reject anything,
so all nine reported clean over nothing:
[9]R-3  every signing identity is enumerated and applied    -> signing.* on every row
[9]R-4  a release artifact outlives the run that made it    -> artifactFormats + served flag
[9]R-5  release only to declared channels, never a partial  -> this file + aggregatingJob
[9]R-6  every artifact names the gated commit it came from  -> lane.*
[10]D-1 no channel is claimed that is not served            -> platforms x served
[10]D-4 every store channel has a publisher account         -> kind=store + ownerQueue
[10]D-5 store listing metadata generated from the spec      -> storeMetadataDir
[10]D-9 what is live on which channel, machine-answerable   -> deploymentEnvironment
[10]D-10 each store channel has a repeatable submission path -> submittable
🔴 THE ONE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FILE MEAN ANYTHING: `served` IS THE GATE, NOT MEMBERSHIP.
A row here is NOT a claim that the factory ships to that channel. Rows exist for channels that are
deferred, so their researched facts (formats, identities, toolchain floors, real costs) are recorded
once instead of rediscovered at submission time. Only `served: true` licenses a claim in
sites/_shared/_data/apps.json. Adding "windows" to an app's `platforms` array fails the build today
precisely because both windows rows exist and neither is served.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-channel-register.mjs:
· every apps.json `platforms` value resolves to a SERVED row here          [R-5, D-1]
· every SERVED row's platforms are claimed by a real app — a served channel nobody ships to
is the 'six platforms' lie growing back                                  [R-5, cut 5 corollary]
· every SERVED row with a real keyKind carries a NAMED identity and a DATED restore drill
(the row's own `required` flag cannot waive it — hardened 2026-07-31), plus a lane
that resolves to a real workflow JOB, a deployment-environment template, and a pinned
toolchain floor                                                          [R-3, R-4, R-6, D-9]
· `artifactFormats` and `minimumToolchain` are non-empty arrays of non-empty STRINGS, and a row's
formats are COMPARED TO WHAT ITS LANE BUILDS: a served row whose lane emits none of the formats
it accepts FAILS, a deferred row's gap PRINTS every run (added 2026-07-31 — before it, the
'.aab required, `flutter build apk` shipped' contradiction two rows down could never fail a
build)                                                                    [R-3, R-4]
· `keyKinds` below IS the vocabulary rows are validated against — the guard derives it from this
file instead of carrying its own copy, so deleting the dictionary or renaming an entry out from
under the rows still using it fails                                       [F-2]
· every `kind: store` row names an `ownerQueue` id. SHAPE ONLY: CI cannot read OWNER_QUEUE.md
(see below), but a store row with no id at all is checkable here          [D-4]
· the aggregating job's `needs` equals every other job in its workflow — the 'never a partial
set' half, which is how a new platform job silently stops being required  [R-5]
· disqualified channels are named with the LOCKED ADR that killed them, and printed every run
· COVERAGE LOST when the register is absent, empty, or has nothing served   [D-1 requires loud]
⚠️ `ownerQueue` IDS ARE DATA, NOT AN ASSERTION. company/ is gitignored (.gitignore:15) and is not
in the public repo, so no CI guard can read OWNER_QUEUE.md. [10]D-4's machine limbs as written are
unimplementable in CI for that reason — they are a LOCAL check. Recorded here so the ids are at
least in one place a guard could reach if company/ ever ships.
⚠️ MINIMUM TOOLCHAIN NAMES KEYS, NOT VALUES. [pipeline F-2] says every version is declared once;
duplicating '3.44.8' here would make this file the second declaration and the first to drift. So a
row names the tooling/versions.json KEYS that gate it, and the guard asserts they are pinned there.
A served row naming an unpinned key FAILS; a deferred row naming one PRINTS — which is how Apple's
Xcode 26 floor stays visible without blocking CI on an owner-deferred channel.

_why: [R-5] 'a release either produces the complete artifact set for its declared channels or produces
nothing.' The aggregating job is that half. It is already built and correct — it fails on any
`failure` or `cancelled` across `needs.*` — but nothing checked that `needs` still LISTS every
job. Add a seventh platform job and forget one line, and the aggregate goes green over a set it
no longer covers, which is this repo's single most repeated failure wearing a YAML hat.

keyKinds.none: the channel signs for us — nothing of ours can be lost
keyKinds.upload-key: we sign the upload; the store holds the real app signing key (Play App Signing)
keyKinds.app-signing-key: we hold the key end users' installs are bound to — loss is unrecoverable
keyKinds.distribution-certificate: an Apple distribution certificate + provisioning profile
keyKinds.code-signing-certificate: a CA-issued certificate chaining to a trusted root — a real recurring cost
keyKinds.own-signing-key: our own detached signature, no gatekeeper verifying it for us

channels.name: Web (Cloudflare Pages, app subdomain)

signing.custody: n/a — the web channel signs nothing. TLS is Cloudflare's certificate, not ours.

restoreDrill.note: No identity of ours exists to restore. This is why [9]R-3 is not revenue-critical: the one live channel has no signing identity to lose.

notes: The only served channel, and deliberately so — 39-CHASSIS §4 cut 5 defers native platform
folders, the per-platform deploy workflows and tooling/release/ until an app proves it converts.
Verified live: apps.json carries subly platforms:["web"] status:"live"; the deployment ledger
holds subly-web.
⚠️ deploy-web.yml builds with --pwa-strategy=none, so there is no service worker and no offline
support on the one platform the $0 desktop story rests on. Recorded, not fixed here.

channels.name: Google Play

signing.custody: recorded in the private SSoT (OWNER_QUEUE S-4 / reconciliation #25). Redacted here 2026-07-31: a public register must say THAT custody is recorded, never WHERE a key lives or how it is protected.

restoreDrill.note: NEVER DRILLED. The file has existed since 11 Jun 2026 and is wired to nothing. OWNER_QUEUE S-5 still says 'generate' — reconciliation decision #25 rewords it to 'adopt or replace, then drill a restore'. Unexecuted.

deferral.reason: 39-CHASSIS §4 cut 5 — native store work is deferred until an app proves it converts strangers.
deferral.alsoBlockedBy: Play Organization needs a D-U-N-S (OWNER_QUEUE A-3, waiting by choice). Play Individual needs none but costs the 12-tester / 14-day closed-testing window.

notes: 🔴 TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS PLAY REFUSES WHAT CI BUILDS TODAY, and the register records both.
FORMAT: developer.android.com/guide/app-bundle — 'From August 2021, new apps are required to
publish with the Android App Bundle on Google Play.' build-platforms.yml runs `flutter build apk`.
SIGNING: apps/subly/android/app/build.gradle.kts resolves `release` to signingConfigs debug.
So the green 'Android builds' tick is a proof about an artifact Play rejects twice over.
The key we hold is an UPLOAD key, not the app signing key — different loss consequences.

channels.name: Apple App Store (iOS)

signing.custody: does not exist — no Apple Developer account (OWNER_QUEUE A-4, DEFERRED by owner). Also needs an ASC API key and Team Agent account recovery (FIDO2 + Legacy Contact, G-48).

restoreDrill.note: Nothing to drill until the account exists.

deferral.reason: 🔒 DEFERRED by owner (OWNER_QUEUE A-4) until non-Apple revenue exists — no Apple device, and no Apple ORGANIZATION path exists for a sole proprietorship (Apple: enroll as an individual).
deferral.alsoBlockedBy: No Apple hardware for device testing, VoiceOver accessibility, or submission.

notes: 🔴 UNPINNED TOOLCHAIN FLOOR, ALREADY IN FORCE. developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/
(fetched 2026-07-29): apps uploaded to App Store Connect 'must be built with Xcode 26 or later'
— effective 28 April 2026. build-platforms.yml runs on `macos-26` and pins NO Xcode, and
tooling/versions.json has no `xcode` key. The guard prints this gap on every run rather than
failing, because the channel is owner-deferred. versions.json's own $runners_comment names this
exact hazard and the fix it shipped pins the IMAGE LABEL, not the toolchain.

channels.name: Apple App Store (macOS)

signing.custody: does not exist — same Apple Developer account as ios-appstore (OWNER_QUEUE A-4).

restoreDrill.note: Nothing to drill until the account exists.

deferral.reason: 🔒 DEFERRED by owner with ios-appstore (OWNER_QUEUE A-4).
deferral.alsoBlockedBy: Notarization is a separate step from signing and needs the same account.

notes: A separate submission from iOS even though it shares an account, which is why it is a separate
row: one App Store Connect record per platform, one metadata tree, one review outcome.
Same Xcode 26 floor as ios-appstore.

channels.name: Microsoft Store

signing.custody: n/a — the Store re-signs the submitted MSIX. Microsoft Store Policies v7.19 §10.2 makes the developer responsible for certificate acquisition 'unless provided by Microsoft Store signing'.

restoreDrill.note: No key of ours exists on this path. This is what makes Microsoft the cheapest real store channel.

deferral.reason: 39-CHASSIS §4 cut 5 — the SUBMISSION work is deferred. ⚠️ Account REGISTRATION is not deferred and is the fastest real channel: $0, no D-U-N-S required, 2–5 business days.
deferral.alsoBlockedBy: 🔴 ONE-WAY DOOR — publishing as NIKATRU requires a COMPANY account and OWNER_QUEUE A-2 points at Individual. Microsoft: changing Individual to Company is not supported; the only remedy is a second publisher account, which is exactly the related-account posture [10]D-6 and L21 exist to avoid.

notes: 🔴 MSIX PACKAGE IDENTITY IS THIS ROW'S FIELD, not [9]R-7's (stage 3's tripwire bundle routes it
wrongly). It has a real downstream consumer: [13]T-5's Windows `cancelAll` is a NO-OP without it.
Fee is $0 for both account types, but only via storedeveloper.microsoft.com — other entry points
show the legacy paid flow. Company verification accepts a government business registration in
place of a D-U-N-S (GST + Udyam are live), and needs a work email on our own domain.
MS policy 10.5.1: a privacy policy URL is required in Partner Center for any product accessing
personal information — this channel carries its own stage-8 dependency, not just Play's.

channels.name: Windows direct download (dl.nikatru.com)

signing.custody: does not exist — and unlike every other row this one costs real money every year.

restoreDrill.note: No certificate purchased. Nothing to drill.

deferral.reason: 39-CHASSIS §4 cut 5, and it is the more expensive of the two Windows paths.

notes: 🔬 THE SECOND WINDOWS ROW, and it exists because the two paths have OPPOSITE signing answers.
Microsoft Store Policies v7.19 §10.2.9 (non-gaming direct download): 'the binary and all of its
Portable Executable (PE) files must be digitally signed with a code signing certificate that
chains up to a certificate issued by a Certificate Authority (CA) that is part of the Microsoft
Trusted Root Program'. Store = no key; direct = our own cert. Recording both is the whole point
of the register — one 'windows' row would have hidden a recurring cost until submission day.

channels.name: Snap Store

signing.custody: n/a — Canonical hosts and signs the binary.

restoreDrill.note: No key of ours. Cost is a per-app namespace registration, the same one-time shape as Play and MS Store.

deferral.reason: [ADR 015] §2 — native Linux is DEFERRED until there is revenue. The web build already serves Linux users at $0, and Linux is the smallest addressable market with no store payments.

notes: [ADR 015] §3 ranks Snap FIRST when native Linux is built: a real store link, discovery and
silent auto-update; accepts closed source; NO AI-code policy; ingests the prebuilt CI artifact
via `plugin: dump`; bundles libmpv via `stage-packages: [libmpv2]`; must declare
`plugs: [opengl, wayland, x11, audio-playback]`.

channels.name: AppImage from dl.nikatru.com

signing.custody: does not exist — no store gatekeeper verifies this one, so the signature is only worth what our custody of it is worth.

notes: 🔴 [ADR 015] §4 IS A CONSTRAINT ON THIS ROW, not a preference: the AppImage is served from
dl.nikatru.com on R2, NEVER a direct GitHub link. GitHub Releases stays the artifact ORIGIN;
it is not the download button. 'This does not conflict with L12: the invariant is that CI
produces the signed artifact, not where it is served from.'
🔒 [ADR 015] §5: the in-app update check is the LOCKED update mechanism for every non-store
channel — min_supported_version -> mustForceUpdate -> ForceUpdateGate -> AppConfig.updateUrl.
linuxdeploy traces and bundles libmpv.so into the image. No store, no discovery, no silent update.

disqualified.name: Flathub
_tellsWhy: EVERY STRING THAT ADVERTISES THIS CHANNEL, not just its id. `assert-channel-claims.mjs` scans
these tokens case-insensitively over RAW site text. The id alone was not enough, proven by
mutation 2026-07-31: a public surface reading "install the flatpak from your distro store"
passed clean, because `flatpak` is the package FORMAT and `flathub` is the channel id. A reader
cannot tell the difference and neither can a store reviewer. The guard REQUIRES this array —
non-empty and containing the id — so deleting or emptying it FAILS instead of silently
narrowing the scan to the id alone (hardened 2026-07-31 after a mutation proved the old
fallback made exactly that narrowing silent).
⚠️ `.deb` and `apt` are deliberately NOT here: [ADR 015] rejected them as OPTIONS, it did not
disqualify them as channels, and a token that broad would fire on any prose about Linux.
reason: Flathub's requirements page bans AI-generated or AI-assisted code, documentation or any other
content, and says such submissions can be rejected without review with repeat violations risking
a permanent ban. This repo's public git history carries Claude co-author trailers and cannot be
rewritten, so we cannot comply — and a publisher-wide ban is existential against L21's single
store identity. AMENDS lock L12 ('Linux = Flathub first').
⬜ OWNER_QUEUE A-5 still reads PENDING for this channel, and site copy still carries live Flathub
documents instruct a submission a LOCKED ADR forbids. [10]D-4's and [10]D-1's job, not R-5's.

nonChannelSigningIdentities.name: Content-pack Ed25519 signing key
nonChannelSigningIdentities.custody: recorded in [ADR 022] (LOCKED 2026-07-27, private SSoT). Public fact only: `k1` is pinned in packages/core/lib/src/content/pack_verifier.dart. Redacted here 2026-07-31 — seed locations belong in the private record, not a public register.

restoreDrill.note: ⬜ THE OPEN HALF IS THE DRILL, NOT THE KEY. OWNER_QUEUE S-3 records the seed as generated, pinned and printed; what remains is a restore from the paper copy BEFORE the first pack is signed under k1.

notes: Here because reconciliation C10 / decision 2.1 #3 assigned pack-key custody to [9]R-3's register,
and [9]R-3's register is this file. It is not a channel, so it lives outside `channels` rather
than being forced into a shape it does not have.
🔴 [ADR 022] SUPERSEDES THE SHAMIR PROCEDURE FOR THIS KEY: 'Shamir splitting is NOT required'.
G-48's air-gapped -> Shamir-split -> hardware sequence still governs the Android and Apple rows.
⬜ Two unexecuted bookkeeping items, both already decided: OWNER_QUEUE S-3 step (2) still says
'Shamir-split the raw seed' while its own status column records the supersession, and
packages/core/tool/gen_pack_keypair.dart still teaches it in its header ('steps 2 and 4 are not
optional').
